Amir —

Really appreciate the detail and the worksheet. Quick reply to confirm: yes, Redwood supports staged rollouts (canary + regional split) and we have a KV cache migration path that reduces warm-start token costs — we usually model a 60–80% effective cache hit after the first week depending on request similarity.

I attached a short term-sheet that outlines a tiered exchange we typically propose for mid-market customers switching from a provider with an existing committed spend. High-level:
- Pilot (0–$50k/mo): usage pricing with small onboarding credit (one-time) and 30-day pilot SLA
- Production ($50k–$250k/mo): discounted per-token rates, up to 12% migration credit applied over first 3 billing cycles for announced committed spend
- Enterprise (>$250k/mo): tiered prepay options, dedicated throughput SLAs, and customizable migration buckets (rebates or invoice credits)

Marissa (AE) will pull together an example P&L with modeled per-token numbers and a migration-credit amortization. Can we get a quick call this week to align on the profile assumptions?

Amir — thanks for the RFP and Evelyn for the term-sheet. I ran a rapid model against the worksheet you provided. Below is a conservative starter offer we think maps to CloudWave's ask (numbers illustrative; final quote will be on official letterhead):

Proposed tiered example (per 1M tokens equivalent):
- Pilot: $28 / 1M tokens (no long-term commitment; includes one-off $10k onboarding credit)
- Production: $18 / 1M tokens with a 6-month minimum commitment; 9% migration credit applied as invoice credit across first 3 months
- Enterprise: $12 / 1M tokens (annual commit); migration credit options: either 6% applied monthly over first 6 months or a single upfront credit equivalent to estimated egress/onboarding costs (we'd validate with your billing team)

Notes and assumptions:
- Batching and KV cache assumptions: modeled 40% effective batching and 65% steady-state KV hit for your 2k median; if you can enable heavier batching we can materially lower the Production tier by ~10–15% in modeled cost.
- Pilot to Production conversion: we typically structure a credit holdback until final onboarding verification and SLA acceptance.
- Competitive parity: our Production tier target is positioned below CloudEdge's published blended rate for equivalent throughput (we'll share the specific comparison in the P&L).

Next steps:
1) Sean to run a short perf pilot (3–5 day spike test) to validate latency at your observed load.
2) Marissa to produce a one-page P&L and redlineable term-sheet for procurement.
3) Legal to exchange baseline T&Cs (Marissa, I'll copy your legal contact if/when you want that).
